newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Montague says Busang gives stock filip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Montague says Busang gives stock filip.

text.p: Montague Gold NL on Monday attributed fluctuations in its share price to a high of 46 cents from 18 cents last Tuesday to market speculation about who will own the giant Busang gold project in Indonesia.

Montague is one of a handful of groups threatening legal action unless they are included in negotiations between Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and an Indonesian partner in the project, PT Krueng Gasui, which claims up to 40 percent of Busang.
Montague has so far been barred by Bre-X Minerals Ltd from participating in the talks.
Montague, whose shares last traded at 35 cents on Friday, is investigating whether it has claims against Bre-X and some of its officers, Montague said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
Wayne Kernaghan, company secretary of Montague, told Reuters that Montague along with other companies and individuals will press ahead with legal actions if negotiations are concluded separately.
"Bre-X has so far declined our request to be included in negotiations," Kernaghan said.

Bre-X late last month said it had received a letter from Canadian lawyers acting for Waverly Mining Finance Plc, Montague, Westralian Resources Projects Ltd and William McLucas threatening legal action.
Bre-X said at the time that the claim was "without foundation".
Bre-X is seeking a partner to provide the funds needed to develop the deposit, estimated to hold at least 57 million ounces of gold.
The Indonesian government is pressing Bre-X to link up with one of the world's largest gold mining companies, Barrick Gold Corp and is seeking its own 10 percent stake.
Two members of Indonesian president Suharto's family are involved in the long-running saga.
Kernaghan was doubtful Montague's stock movemment was related to Montague's 0.25 percent net smelter royalty on the Busang One property, saying the royalty was worth only about A$100,000.
